problem.problem:
Charlie is young. Erin is blue. Erin is green. Fiona is big. Fiona is green. Gary is blue. Gary is green. All red things are furry. All furry things are red. Young things are red. If something is smart and not red then it is not green. All furry things are green. If something is red and green then it is blue. If something is young and big then it is smart. If something is blue and green then it is smart. Blue, red things are smart.

Determine whether the following statement is true, false, or unknown:
Gary is not smart.

Predicates:
Young($x, bool) ::: Is x young?
Blue($x, bool) ::: Is x blue?
Green($x, bool) ::: Is x green?
Big($x, bool) ::: Is x big?
Red($x, bool) ::: Is x red?
Furry($x, bool) ::: Is x furry?
Smart($x, bool) ::: Is x smart?

Facts:
Young(Charlie, True) ::: Charlie is young.
Blue(Erin, True) ::: Erin is blue.
Green(Erin, True) ::: Erin is green.
Big(Fiona, True) ::: Fiona is big.
Green(Fiona, True) ::: Fiona is green.
Blue(Gary, True) ::: Gary is blue.
Green(Gary, True) ::: Gary is green.

Rules:
Red($x, True) >>> Furry($x, True) ::: All red things are furry.
Furry($x, True) >>> Red($x, True) ::: All furry things are red.
Young($x, True) >>> Red($x, True) ::: Young things are red.
Smart($x, True) && !Red($x, True) >>> !Green($x, True) ::: If something is smart and not red then it is not green.
Furry($x, True) >>> Green($x, True) ::: All furry things are green.
Red($x, True) && Green($x, True) >>> Blue($x, True) ::: If something is red and green then it is blue.
Young($x, True) && Big($x, True) >>> Smart($x, True) ::: If something is young and big then it is smart.
Blue($x, True) && Green($x, True) >>> Smart($x, True) ::: If something is blue and green then it is smart.
Blue($x, True) && Red($x, True) >>> Smart($x, True) ::: Blue, red things are smart.

Query:
!Smart(Gary, True) ::: Gary is not smart.
